US-01.title: Sign in, sign out and open the correct dashboard
criteria: Active users reach the correct role dashboard; invalid/inactive users are denied with a generic message.
Protected APIs check active sessions and roles even on direct requests.
Logout invalidates the session and subsequent protected requests fail.
Use Django sessions; deployment session cookies are HttpOnly, Secure and host-only; login and writes require CSRF.

US-02.title: View and update my student profile
criteria: Only the signed-in student can read/update their own profile.
Valid phone changes persist after refresh; reject empty/malformed input with field messages.
Phone-only student edits are the proposed baseline pending confirmation; reject protected-field updates to name, SRN, hostel, room and role.

US-03.title: Publish and read notices, contacts, information and rules
criteria: Students see active notices in the current active window, hostel information, contacts and rules.
Only the Director and explicitly authorized content staff create/edit/deactivate content.
Reject missing titles and invalid active ranges.
Keep stable rule IDs; deactivate referenced rules instead of deleting them.

US-04.title: Manage authorized users, settings and Director summaries
US-04.deps: US-01; US-06, US-07, US-14, US-16 for summaries
criteria: Director-only management endpoints activate/deactivate accounts, assign permitted roles and maintain approved settings.
Deactivated accounts lose access, including existing sessions on subsequent requests.
Permit only one active Chief Warden; support that Chief supervising multiple wardens and student-to-warden assignment.
Counts for pending leave, attendance by session, open complaints and unpaid fees match owning-module records; empty sets return zero; do not edit source records through reports.

US-05.title: Submit and track a leave request
criteria: Valid dates and non-empty reason create a Pending request with ID and submission time.
Reject end before start and missing input.
Derive student identity and assigned warden on the server; show assigned requests to that warden.
Students see only their own request history.

US-06.title: Review leave and escalate to the Chief Warden
criteria: Only the assigned Warden decides Pending: Approve, Reject or Escalate.
Only Chief Warden finalizes Escalated requests.
Approved/Rejected are final and immutable; concurrent/repeated decisions cannot overwrite them.
Append actor, server timestamp, previous/new status and remarks for each transition; student sees status and decision history.

US-07.title: Configure attendance sessions and submit one-time location attendance
criteria: Authorized wardens configure start/end, centre and positive radius; end follows start.
Server validates inclusive time window, distance and approved accuracy threshold; valid in-range submissions yield one accepted record.
Closed/outside-range/denied/unavailable/low-accuracy cases do not create accepted attendance.
PostgreSQL uniqueness and atomic handling prevent concurrent or retry duplicate accepted records per student/session.

Request one geolocation sample only after Submit; no watchPosition, background polling or retained raw student coordinates in DB/logs/history. Retain time and check result only; browser location is not tamper-proof.

US-08.title: Record deviations and calculate active weightage
criteria: Authorized wardens record student, existing rule, copied rule weightage, remarks, actor and server time; students cannot write.
Sum active entries only, excluding deactivated entries.
Changing the source rule must not rewrite historical copied weightage.
Student read-only history is owner-scoped; staff reads are authorization-scoped.

US-09.title: Display and update study-room Open/Closed status
criteria: Accept only Open or Closed.
Show latest status, optional timings/message and update time.
Only Director or explicitly permitted staff update; record updating user.
No booking, seats, reservation API or student edit action. Preserve legacy UC-02; UC-11 is a proposed controlled correction, not an approved change.

US-10.title: Assign and view allocated laundry day
criteria: Laundry Staff assigns one valid current weekday per student.
Student sees read-only allocated day or Not assigned.
Students cannot select/reserve/modify a day through UI or API.
Future allocation changes preserve historical handover/collection details.

US-11.title: Record clothes received by laundry
criteria: Laundry Staff records valid student, non-empty item details and positive whole-number count.
Create Received state with server time and receiving actor.
Reject missing fields, fractional, zero and negative counts.
Student reads only personal records; store historical allocation context so changes do not rewrite the past.

US-12.title: Record collection and retain laundry history
criteria: Only existing Received records can become Collected.
Keep original item details, handover time/actor and append collection time/actor.
Repeated collection is idempotent: no new record and no overwriting original completion time.
Student cannot change status or read another student history.

US-13.title: Submit and track maintenance complaint
criteria: Use server student profile room plus valid category and non-empty description.
Create Open complaint with ID; invalid input yields field errors and no record.
Own list/detail persists after refresh.
No cross-student reads or modifications.

US-14.title: Assign complaints and update progress
criteria: Director assigns to active Maintenance Staff.
Only assigned staff or Director perform permitted transitions Open → In Progress → Resolved.
Append actor, server time and remarks per transition; no silent revert of resolved complaint.
Student sees current status and history but cannot edit assignment or staff remarks.

US-15.title: Manage mess allocation and active coupons
criteria: Only Mess Staff creates/updates allocations and coupons.
Student sees current personal assigned mess and active currently valid coupons.
Reject invalid date range and missing coupon code.
No cross-student access or student writes; no ordering, QR redemption or billing.

US-16.title: View fees and verify test payment results
criteria: Separate FeeDue and PaymentAttempt; fixed-precision amount/currency; initiate for server-calculated amount.
Only verified server-side matching fee/order/amount/currency success marks fee Paid.
Failed/cancelled attempts leave Unpaid; unverified result stays Pending.
Unique provider reference plus atomic update prevents duplicate success even on concurrent callbacks/retries.
Keep failure/cancellation/pending attempt history; no credentials, card/UPI PINs or real funds; provider-hosted test checkout only. Simulation requires faculty approval and explicit labeling.

US-17.title: Baseline architecture and scaffold monorepo
criteria: Working Next.js and Django/DRF skeletons with health response.
Architecture/deployment diagrams show browser → Next.js → Django → PostgreSQL, external payment/location and separate CI path.
Record stack revision and duplicate UC correction proposal without changing FR IDs.
All four members review and can run the skeleton.

US-18.title: Agree models, permissions and API contracts
criteria: Reviewed data design covers all profile/information/study/laundry/leave/attendance/complaint/mess/fee/deviation entities.
Specify endpoint inputs, outputs, roles, ownership and errors; choose custom user model before initial migrations.
Each owner supplies portable migrations; clean SQLite quick-mode and PostgreSQL runs; prove attendance/payment uniqueness on PostgreSQL.
All four owners approve shared schema and permission matrix.

US-19.title: Provide reproducible Docker environment and demo data
criteria: Clean clone starts frontend/API/PostgreSQL from README via Compose.
Named PostgreSQL volume preserves data across recreation.
Exclude secrets, SQLite, dependencies and build outputs from Git and every Docker context.
Fictional demo accounts for all seven roles; seeding refuses production by default; every member verifies login.

US-20.title: Gate PRs and deploy reviewed releases
criteria: PRs run lint/scanners/PostgreSQL backend tests/frontend tests/builds without deployment secrets.
Branch protection and independent review block failed required checks; empty tests are not success.
Trusted successful main push deploys staging for the same source SHA; wait for readiness/version and smoke success.
Only approved production promotion of the same reviewed SHA; document manual approval alternative if plan lacks reviewers.
Preserve real CI/coverage/scanner artifacts including failures; no queued-deploy-as-success or host auto-deploy bypass.

US-21.title: Validate usability and assemble final handoff
criteria: Chrome/Edge/Firefox checks cover labels, actionable errors, keyboard and phone/tablet/desktop usability.
Final report traces every FR to actual stories, PRs, tests and evidence.
15-minute presentation/rehearsal includes each member explaining and demonstrating owned functionality.
List unfinished work/defects honestly; never label unbuilt stories implemented.

US-22.title: Maintain validation and verify access rules
criteria: Every FR, NFR, SEC and BR has cases with preconditions/input/expected result.
Seeded role, session, CSRF and ownership checks cover all personal modules, only against own local/staging app.
Attendance boundary/retry cases on PostgreSQL; no retained raw location.
Fill actual results only after execution; link failed cases to observed bugs and rerun. Tests remain Not Run initially.

US-23.title: Run integrated workflows and reliability checks
criteria: Critical Playwright login/leave/laundry/complaint flows across integrated app.
PostgreSQL tests prove attendance/payment retries and concurrency produce no duplicate accepted/success records.
Performance baseline proposed: 20 signed-in synthetic users, 100 warm visits, p95 navigation-to-usable ≤3s; approval required before target is binding.
Record browser/env/dataset/SHA/time/observations and failures; cover mess/payment/deviation with repeatable manual cases where appropriate.

US-24.title: Verify recovery and complete maintenance guidance
criteria: Restore synthetic PostgreSQL backup into separate database and verify expected counts.
Record/test known-good frontend/API rollback after checking schema compatibility; app rollback does not reverse migrations.
Retest sandbox success/failure/pending/duplicate payment acceptance with no real funds/data.
Name maintainers, weekly dependency review, backups, incident/bug triage and recovery steps; no dumps/secrets in repository.
